text:
Adam Fox has 27 points in 24 games, a career-best start, and the Norris Trophy conversation still mostly happens somewhere else. Two outlets made the same case this week (Blue Line Station and Yahoo Sports both argued he deserves more Norris attention), and our numbers back them up.

With Fox on the ice at five on five, the Rangers get 59% of the expected goals, the share of chance quality, and that is more than ten points better than they do without him. He plays nearly 23 minutes a night, and lately closer to 24. Evolving-Hockey rated him ninth among 215 defensemen last season, with impact at both ends: his team creates more with him out there and gives up less.

The odd part is that his numbers could be better. The Rangers have scored 6.4 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which is the biggest reason his points sit where they do. He has one goal in his last ten games and nine assists, including a four-game point streak. If the finishing around him catches up to the chances he is helping create, the voters will have a harder time looking past him.
